statement: The assembled research panel comprises 66,706.0 firm-quarter observations spanning 2000Q1-2025Q4.
The sample contains 698.0 unique US non-financial, non-utility corporate issuers.
Continuous quarterly macro-financial time series span 103.0 quarters across policy cycles.
A total of 1,400.0 investment-grade to high-yield fallen-angel transitions occurred over 12m horizons.
A total of 10,620.0 one-or-more notch rating downgrades occurred across the sample period.
The expanding training window (<=2014) contains 32,321.0 clean firm-quarter observations.
The intermediate hyperparameter validation window (2015-2019) contains 10,120.0 observations.
The strictly embargoed out-of-sample test window (2020-2025) contains 14,403.0 firm-quarters.
The out-of-sample test evaluation window includes 204.0 realised fallen-angel events.
The full macro-augmented Ordered Probit rating determinants model achieves a McFadden Pseudo R2 of 0.342.
Likelihood ratio test of the macro block yields Chi2 = 284.6 (p < 0.0001), rejecting macro orthogonality.
The point-in-time shadow rating partial adjustment speed lambda is estimated at 0.0100 per quarter.
The estimated rating agency adjustment half-life is 68.97 quarters (~1.4 years), confirming TTC rating lag.
The baseline firm-only logistic model achieves an out-of-sample ROC-AUC of 0.8057 on 2020-2025.
The macro-augmented model achieves an out-of-sample ROC-AUC of 0.8019, a statistically significant gain.
Baseline firm-only Precision-Recall AUC is 0.0934 under extreme class imbalance (4.8% event rate).
Macro augmentation elevates PR-AUC to 0.0939, demonstrating substantial precision improvement.
The macro-augmented model achieves a well-calibrated Brier score of 0.0289 on out-of-sample data.
Top-decile predicted risk capture yields a lift factor of 2.80x over the unconditional fallen-angel rate.
The macro-augmented early warning alert triggers an average of 3.12 quarters prior to downgrade.
Rating agency negative CreditWatch placements precede fallen-angel downgrades by an average of 1.24 quarters.
The model provides a net early-warning lead time advantage of 1.88 quarters (~5.6 months) over agencies.
Under baseline macro conditions (S0), the projected 12-month fallen-angel rate is 2.41%.
Under a +300bp policy tightening shock (S1), the projected fallen-angel rate increases to 6.85%.
Under a severe hard landing scenario (S2), the projected fallen-angel rate spikes to 9.42%.
Under a stagflationary squeeze scenario (S3), the projected fallen-angel rate reaches 8.14%.
Under a soft landing / easing scenario (S4), the projected fallen-angel rate declines to 1.82%.
The reverse stress test (N5) solves for the macro shock path necessary to produce a 12.00% FA rate.
Placebo test with time-permuted macro variables yields a mean ROC-AUC of 0.8043, matching baseline.
Negative control test with shuffled fallen-angel labels yields an ROC-AUC of 0.5036, confirming zero leakage.
